name: JEV-27B-VL (repo AutoTrust-Decider-Pro-Vision-27B)

lineage.how_derived: System 1: LoRA adapter plus decision head trained on text only (distillation corpus jev-distill-corpus-v3, labels from the hosted TypeSafe Jev 1.13); System 2 is the unmodified Qwen3.8-27B

purpose: One decision model instead of a ranking team: typed decisions (yes/no, pick one of 2-256 options, rate 0-5) over text and images with calibrated probabilities (System 1), escalating to normal thinking generation (System 2) when confidence is low (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE read (Apache License 2.0); base Qwen3.8-27B is Apache-2.0.

architecture.kind: Qwen3.8-27B vision-language with a LoRA System 1 adapter and a 255-way decision head; served with vLLM plus a /v1/decide endpoint
architecture.why_this_design: card: System 1 gives a calibrated probability per option in one forward pass (about half a second for a ranking), System 2 reasons only below a confidence threshold; the vision encoder is unchanged and the adapter was trained on text only

benchmarks.name: Jev Decision Index 0.3 Vision board, Full score
benchmarks.variant: board by a community Space; as quoted on the card (rank 1 of 20; public 72.78, private 66.86, ECE 0.019; Solomon v1.1 67.66, Xor 1.2 64.30)

benchmarks.name: six public decision benchmarks, mean
benchmarks.variant: JEV-27B text; TypeSafe Jev 1.13 hosted 83.85, NeoHorse-Jev-4B 77.70

strengths: A decision model reads a state (text, JSON, images) and a schema of typed questions and returns calibrated probabilities for every option in one forward pass; it does not generate text.
zero-shot image decisions although the adapter saw only text
calibration error 0.019 on the vision board
weaknesses: benchmark claims lean on the vendor's own demo corpus and a labelled-by-teacher distillation (KL to the teacher's distributions)
56 GB BF16 with no quantized release
best_for: ranking, routing, moderation and judging steps; computer-use step selection from screenshots as demonstrated by the vendor
avoid_for: chat and coding as a replacement for a worker model
soft.maturity: 992k downloads and 5.8k likes within seven weeks, the highest traction among the decision models; repo renamed (card header says JEV-27B-VL)

tona_fit.reason: Top of the community vision decision board with permissive Apache and an unmodified generator behind it, but a 27B BF16 decision classifier is a pipeline component, not a worker; no quantized form. Worth a look as a local router/judge if Tona adds typed-decision endpoints.

open_questions: why traction is far above the other decision models (download counts not explained)
independent confirmation of the board score (the board page itself was not opened)
